item.title: DPRK Contagious Interview campaign hides OTTERCOOKIE malware in trojanized coding challenges
WordPress wp2shell RCE, OpenSSL HollowByte, ViteVenom npm RAT, and Abbott Probe
HollowByte OpenSSL DoS, NadMesh AI Botnet, and GoldenEyeDog DigiCert Breach
Fairlife Ransomware Halt, Windows LegacyHive Zero-Day, and EU Android AI Access Order
CISA Warns on Exploited Fortinet FortiSandbox and SharePoint RCE Flaws
WordPress wp2shell RCE, OpenSSL HollowByte, and DPRK Contagious Interview Lead Threat Digest
item.content:encoded:
New wp2shell WordPress Core Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code — Must Read

WordPress patched a critical pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in core affecting versions 6.9.0–6.9.4 and 7.0.0–7.0.1, where anonymous requests could exploit the REST API batch endpoint on default installs. Site owners should verify they are running 6.9.5 or 7.0.2 rather than relying on auto-updates, since there is no CVE yet and scanners may miss it.

  • WordPress released versions 6.9.5 and 7.0.2 on July 17, 2026, to fix a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in core that anonymous requests could trigger on a default install with no plugins.
  • The affected WordPress versions are 6.9.0 through 6.9.4 and 7.0.0 through 7.0.1, while WordPress 7.1 beta2 also carries the same fix.
  • WordPress described the issue reported by Adam Kues of Assetnote as a REST API batch-route confusion and SQL injection issue leading to remote code execution.
  • No CVE ID or CVSS score had been assigned by July 18, so CVE-based scanners, inventories, and CISA’s KEV catalog would not flag the issue.
  • Searchlight Cyber recommended temporary mitigations that block anonymous access to the batch endpoint, including WAF rules for both /wp-json/batch/v1 and rest_route=/batch/v1, disabling unauthenticated REST API access, or using a drop-in plugin.

CISA Adds Exploited SharePoint RCE Zero-Day CVE-2026-58644 to KEV — Must Read

CISA added a newly patched Microsoft SharePoint Server zero-day, CVE-2026-58644, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming active exploitation, requiring U.S. federal agencies to patch by July 19, 2026. Organizations running on-premises SharePoint should urgently apply updates, verify defenses like AMSI, and check for signs of compromise.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-58644, a newly patched Microsoft SharePoint Server flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and required Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to apply fixes by July 19, 2026.
  • CVE-2026-58644 is a critical deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.8 that allows an unauthorized attacker to execute arbitrary code.
  • Microsoft said the vulnerability can be exploited remotely over the internet and has low attack complexity because attackers need no significant prior system knowledge and can repeatedly succeed with a payload against the vulnerable component.
  • The vulnerability affects Microsoft SharePoint Server Subscription Edition, Microsoft SharePoint Server 2019, and Microsoft SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016.
  • CISA warned that multiple SharePoint Server vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-58644, are being actively exploited to gain unauthorized access to on-premises instances and support post-exploitation activity such as stealing IIS machine keys and deploying malware.

CISA urges immediate action on actively exploited Fortinet flaws — Must Read

CISA says two critical Fortinet FortiSandbox command-injection flaws are being actively exploited and ordered U.S. federal agencies to patch affected systems by July 19. Admins should upgrade FortiSandbox immediately to block unauthenticated remote code execution attacks.

  • CISA ordered U.S. government agencies to prioritize patching two actively exploited critical vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiSandbox, tracked as CVE-2026-39808 and CVE-2026-25089.
  • Fortinet addressed CVE-2026-39808 on April 14 and CVE-2026-25089 on June 9.
  • Successful exploitation of the flaws can allow unauthenticated threat actors to execute unauthorized code remotely through low-complexity command injection attacks that require no user interaction.
  • CISA added the two FortiSandbox vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and required U.S. federal agencies to patch vulnerable instances by July 19.
  • Defused reported on June 16 that attackers had started exploiting multiple Fortinet FortiSandbox vulnerabilities in the wild, including CVE-2026-39808 and CVE-2026-25089.

New North Korean campaign uses fake coding interviews to steal developer credentials — Must Read

Elastic Security Labs uncovered a DPRK-aligned Contagious Interview campaign that lures developers with fake coding challenges and hides OTTERCOOKIE-like malware inside SVG files. Running the trojanized projects can steal browser credentials, crypto wallets, sensitive files and clipboard data while installing a Socket.IO-based remote access backdoor.

  • Elastic Security Labs discovered a new DPRK-aligned Contagious Interview campaign, tracked as REF9403, after a fake recruiter posted a job offer in its community Slack workspace and sent developers a trojanized coding challenge.
  • The trojanized projects hid Base64-encoded payload fragments inside HTML comments across SVG flag images, then reassembled and executed the payload when the project server started.
  • Running the malicious project delivered four OTTERCOOKIE-aligned capabilities: a browser credential and crypto wallet stealer, a file stealer, a Socket.IO-based remote access trojan, and a clipboard stealer.
  • The malware targeted developer machines across Windows, macOS, and Linux by collecting browser data, wallet extension databases, sensitive files, shell histories, cloud and SSH configuration paths, and macOS keychain data.
  • Elastic linked the activity to Contagious Interview based on code similarity, behavior, and infrastructure overlapping with prior reporting on OTTERCOOKIE and related DPRK campaigns.

GoldenEyeDog Subgroup Linked to DigiCert Breach and Code-Signing Certificate Theft — Must Read

Researchers attributed DigiCert’s April 2026 breach to CylindricalCanine, a GoldenEyeDog subgroup that compromised support analyst workstations via a malicious “screenshot” file and stole EV code-signing certificate access. The attackers used the certificates to sign Golden Gh0st RAT/Zhong Stealer malware, highlighting the risk of certificate abuse in malware delivery.

  • Expel attributed the April 2026 DigiCert security incident to CylindricalCanine, described as a subgroup of the Chinese cybercrime group GoldenEyeDog, also known as APT-Q-27, Dragon Breath, and Miuuti Group.
  • DigiCert said the threat actor contacted its support team through a customer chat channel on April 2, 2026, and delivered a ZIP file disguised as a customer screenshot that contained a malicious .scr executable.
  • The attackers compromised two DigiCert support analyst workstations and used a customer-support portal function to access initialization codes for approved but pending EV Code Signing certificate orders across a finite set of customer accounts.
  • DigiCert revoked 60 fraudulently obtained certificates, including 27 explicitly linked to the threat actor, and the exploited certificates were used to sign Zhong Stealer malware artifacts.
  • Expel said CylindricalCanine’s attack chain uses phishing files disguised as screenshots, DLL side-loading, and Golden Gh0st RAT, which can steal data, log keystrokes, take screenshots, execute shell commands, and clear Windows Event logs.

New NadMesh Botnet Hunts Exposed AI Services for Cloud Keys and Kubernetes Tokens — Must Read

The new Go-based NadMesh botnet is scanning exposed AI and developer services to steal AWS keys, Kubernetes tokens, Docker credentials, and model/tool access rather than just hijacking compute. Organizations running ComfyUI, Ollama, n8n, Gradio, MCP, Docker, Jenkins, Redis, or similar services should remove them from the public internet, enforce authentication, check persistence paths, and revoke exposed credentials.

  • QiAnXin’s XLab reported that the Go botnet NadMesh appeared in early July and is scanning exposed AI services including ComfyUI, Ollama, n8n, Open WebUI, Langflow, and Gradio.
  • NadMesh collects cloud keys from environment variables, Kubernetes service account tokens, and files such as ~/.aws/config, .env, and ~/.docker/config.json.
  • The operator’s dashboard claimed 3,811 unique AWS keys, while XLab observed distinct source IPs pushing NadMesh rise to about 139 per day in the first week of July.
  • XLab’s observed exploit traffic was led by docker_containers_api_rce at 30.31% and jenkins_scripttext_rce at 22.28%, while mcp_cmd_execute appeared in the smaller unlabeled tail at 0.78%.
  • The article advises operators of exposed services to place them behind authentication or remove them from the public internet, check listed persistence paths, isolate infected hosts, and revoke credentials the host could access.

New GoSerpent Malware Targets Southeast Asian Governments and Diplomats for Espionage — Must Read

Kaspersky uncovered GoSerpent, a previously undocumented Go-based backdoor used since late 2025 to spy on Southeast Asian government and diplomatic entities, harvest sensitive files, dump credentials, and enable proxy access for long-term espionage. The campaign shows overlaps with the APAC-focused TetrisPhantom actor and involved follow-on tools for staged data collection and exfiltration.

  • Kaspersky discovered a previously undocumented malware called GoSerpent that has been used since late 2025 to target government and diplomatic entities in Southeast Asia for long-term access and intelligence gathering.
  • GoSerpent contacts an external command-and-control server, supports encrypted communications, and can deploy secondary tools for sensitive data collection and credential dumping.
  • The campaign used tools including ThumbcacheService for file collection, Mimikatz for LSASS credential dumping, QuarksDumpLocalHash for extracting local account password hashes, and later Stowaway, TmcLoader, and TmcPayload for proxying, remote access, and exfiltration.
  • Kaspersky said the campaign shares targeting, technical capabilities, and operational overlaps with TetrisPhantom, a threat actor previously documented as targeting government entities in the Asia-Pacific region.
  • Cyderes Howler Cell also detailed a separate DoNot Team cyber espionage operation targeting Bangladesh’s military and defence establishments through spear-phishing emails carrying a malicious RTF document.

Abbott Laboratories probes two cyber incidents amid extortion claims — Should Read

Abbott Laboratories is investigating two cyber incidents: confirmed unauthorized access to legacy Exact Sciences systems in its Cancer Diagnostics business claimed by ShinyHunters, and a separate alleged LabCentral portal breach. Abbott says operations, product availability, and patient services are unaffected, while the attackers claim they stole large amounts of sensitive data that has not been independently verified.

  • Abbott Laboratories is investigating unauthorized access to a limited number of internal legacy Exact Sciences systems in its Cancer Diagnostics business.
  • Abbott said the Cancer Diagnostics incident does not affect business operations, product availability, manufacturing or lab operations, its ability to serve patients, or other Abbott businesses and systems.
  • ShinyHunters claimed it accessed Abbott through a mid-June vishing attack that compromised a Microsoft Entra single sign-on account and allowed access to internal systems.
  • ShinyHunters claimed it stole data from Microsoft Entra, ServiceNow, SharePoint, Databricks, and Coupa, including internal documents, contracts, customer information, and large datasets containing personal and medical-related information, but BleepingComputer has not independently verified those claims.
  • Abbott is also investigating a separate potential incident involving its LabCentral customer portal, but said the portal contains publicly available technical product reference documents and does not contain proprietary, sensitive customer, or business information.

ACR Stealer Uses ClickFix Lures to Steal Browser Tokens and Microsoft 365 Files — Should Read

ACR Stealer campaigns are using ClickFix lures that trick users into pasting commands into Windows Run, leading to theft of browser passwords, session tokens, Microsoft 365 files, and synced OneDrive/SharePoint data. Because stolen tokens remain valid after password resets, defenders should revoke tokens and block the paste-and-run execution path.

  • Microsoft reported that ACR Stealer activity increased across customer environments from late April to mid-June and that campaigns are using ClickFix lures to steal browser credentials, authentication tokens, and sensitive documents.
  • The fileless delivery chain starts when a pasted command launches mshta.exe to retrieve remote HTA content, then uses scripts and a JPEG-hosted payload to execute malware in memory.
  • ACR Stealer targets Chrome and Edge data stores, uses DPAPI to decrypt saved passwords, cookies, and tokens, and also steals PDFs from the Desktop and Downloads folders.
  • A second delivery chain pulls a DLL from a WebDAV share, uses obfuscated PowerShell and a bundled pythonw.exe, persists through a hidden scheduled task, and clears PowerShell history.
  • Microsoft’s remediation guidance says suspected victims should isolate affected hosts, rotate credentials, revoke tokens, and check outbound connections to remote shares and image-hosting services.

New Windows LegacyHive zero-day gives hackers admin privileges — Should Read

A researcher released a proof-of-concept Windows zero-day called LegacyHive that can let standard users gain admin-level code execution by abusing the Windows User Profile Service. Microsoft has not yet assigned a CVE or issued a fix, though the public PoC was partially restricted to reduce easy exploitation.

  • A security researcher using the handle Nightmare Eclipse released a proof-of-concept exploit called LegacyHive for an unpatched Windows User Profile Service vulnerability.
  • The LegacyHive exploit can allow attackers to escalate privileges on up-to-date Windows systems, but the released proof of concept was modified to require additional credentials.
  • Will Dormann tested the exploit and said successful exploitation could let non-admin users modify the classes registry hive and gain automatic code execution when an admin account logs into the compromised system.
  • Kevin Beaumont confirmed that the LegacyHive exploit works and published Microsoft Defender for Endpoint detection queries for it.
  • Microsoft had not assigned a CVE ID to the LegacyHive vulnerability at the time of the article, and a Microsoft spokesperson was not immediately available for comment.

OpenSSL HollowByte Flaw Could Freeze Server Memory with 11-Byte TLS Requests — Should Read

Okta disclosed an OpenSSL flaw dubbed HollowByte that lets an attacker force unpatched TLS servers to retain memory with tiny 11-byte requests, potentially causing denial of service. OpenSSL quietly fixed it in June releases without a CVE or advisory, making it harder for organizations to know whether they are protected.

  • Okta's Red Team disclosed HollowByte, an OpenSSL denial-of-service bug where an 11-byte TLS handshake request can make an unpatched server allocate up to 131 KB of memory for a message body that never arrives.
  • Okta said glibc systems it tested did not return the freed OpenSSL buffers to the kernel after connections closed, allowing memory fragmentation to persist until the process restarts.
  • OpenSSL fixed HollowByte in releases 4.0.1, 3.6.3, 3.5.7, 3.4.6, and 3.0.21 on June 9, but did not assign a CVE, issue an advisory, or mention the fix in release notes or the changelog.
  • Okta's NGINX testing reportedly caused a 1 GB server to be OOM-killed with 547 MB frozen in fragments and locked up 25% of memory on a 16 GB server without exceeding connection limits.
  • The fix covers TLS only, while the article states that the DTLS handshake path still sizes its buffer from the peer-declared length in OpenSSL 4.0.1.

Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages Use Blockchain C2 to Deliver a RAT — Should Read

Researchers found seven malicious npm packages impersonating Vite tooling that use resilient blockchain-based command-and-control infrastructure to deliver a remote access trojan. Developers who installed them should remove the packages, audit systems, rotate credentials, and check shell profile files for persistence.

  • Cybersecurity researchers discovered seven malicious npm packages targeting developers in the Vite frontend tooling ecosystem as part of a software supply chain attack.
  • Checkmarx named the campaign ViteVenom and linked it to an expansion of ChainVeil, attributing the activity to a threat actor called SuccessKey.
  • The packages were published between June 29 and July 3, 2026, and used scoped names intended to impersonate the @vitejs/* namespace.
  • The malicious code runs when imported and retrieves later-stage payloads through blockchain-based infrastructure involving Tron, Aptos, and Binance Smart Chain.
  • Users who installed the packages are advised to remove them immediately, audit dependencies, rotate all credentials, and check .bashrc, .zshrc, and .profile for unauthorized modifications.

Ernst & Young discloses data breach after support system hack — Should Read

Ernst & Young is notifying clients that a third-party support ticket system used by its IT staff was accessed by an unauthorized party, who downloaded documents that may contain client tax-related personal and financial information. EY says it has secured the system, notified law enforcement, and is offering affected clients 24 months of Experian identity monitoring.

  • Ernst & Young is notifying customers of a data breach caused by the compromise of a third-party support ticket system used by its IT personnel.
  • The company determined that an unauthorized third party accessed the support platform between March 28 and April 12 and downloaded multiple documents.
  • The exposed information included certain personal and financial data contained in or used to prepare tax filings, but the specific data types remain unclear.
  • Ernst & Young has not disclosed how many customers were affected or whether the incident impacts only U.S. customers or customers in other countries.
  • Ernst & Young says it secured its systems, notified federal law enforcement, and is offering affected clients 24 months of identity monitoring and restoration services through Experian.

E.U. Orders Google to Open Android Mic, Camera and Screen to Rival AI Assistants — Should Read

The European Commission ordered Google to make Android’s powerful AI-assistant capabilities, including access to the mic, camera, screen, wake word, and app automation, available to rival assistants by Android 18 or August 2027. Google warns this could weaken device security and privacy, but the EU says access must be user-consented and subject to limited safeguards.

  • The European Commission ordered Google to give rival AI assistants the same reach into Android as Gemini, including access to the camera, microphone, screen contents, wake word functionality, and the ability to drive other apps in the background.
  • Google must implement the Android interoperability measures in the next major Android release, Android 18, and by 1 August 2027 at the latest.
  • The Android decision covers 11 operating system features, with Google allowed to require certification for five restricted features but barred from restricting access to six others, including ambient data, always-on hotword detection, and background execution.
  • For the restricted features, Google must create a Qualified AI Assistant Programme and allow third-party Trusted Certification Authorities to certify assistants free of charge under terms that must be reasonable, non-discriminatory, and cleared with the Commission before changes.
  • A second European Commission decision requires Google to provide anonymised Search query, click, and ranking data to rival search engines and AI chatbots that do search for a cost-based fee.

White House Launches Gold Eagle Initiative to Manage Surge in AI-Discovered Vulnerabilities — Should Read

The White House launched the Gold Eagle clearinghouse to coordinate AI-discovered software vulnerabilities, but has disclosed little about its staffing, governance, funding, or how it will actually help overwhelmed maintainers validate and patch findings. The key risk is that AI may produce vulnerabilities faster than the existing ecosystem can process them, and Gold Eagle has not yet shown it can solve that bottleneck.

  • The White House launched the Gold Eagle initiative as a central clearinghouse to triage AI-discovered vulnerabilities, coordinate software scanning, validate reported flaws, and prioritize patches across federal systems, critical infrastructure, and open source software.
  • Gold Eagle was publicly announced on July 14 after being launched internally by July 2 to meet a deadline in President Trump’s June executive order on AI security.
  • The White House said Gold Eagle has begun receiving and prioritizing vulnerabilities and coordinating verification of scanning results, but it has not named participating companies or open source organizations, disclosed how many findings are in the system, or identified patches completed through it.
  • The initiative is meant to address a growing bottleneck in which AI tools can find large numbers of possible software flaws faster than maintainers, vendors, and government agencies can validate, disclose, patch, and distribute fixes.
  • The administration has not explained Gold Eagle’s day-to-day operations, staffing, funding, governance, prioritization criteria, or how it will work alongside existing vulnerability programs such as the CVE program, the National Vulnerability Database, and CISA disclosure efforts.

Dairy company Fairlife suspends production in US after cyber incident — Should Read

Fairlife, Coca-Cola’s dairy unit, temporarily halted U.S. production after detecting a ransomware intrusion, though it says product quality and safety were not affected. The company is still investigating the scope of the incident and has notified law enforcement.

  • A ransomware attack forced Coca-Cola Company’s Fairlife dairy unit to temporarily halt production in the United States.
  • Coca-Cola said Fairlife detected the intrusion on Thursday and that the full scope of the incident is not yet known.
  • Coca-Cola said product quality and safety were not impacted, and Fairlife’s operations in Canada were not affected.
  • An internal investigation is ongoing, and law enforcement has been notified.
  • Coca-Cola did not name the ransomware group behind the incident or announce any breach of corporate or consumer information.

US charges two over laundering $43 million from investment fraud — Should Read

U.S. prosecutors charged Zhuoying Chen and Haojie Zhang with laundering at least $43 million stolen from cyber investment scam victims through 140 bank accounts tied to shell companies. If convicted of money laundering conspiracy, they each face up to 20 years in prison.

  • U.S. prosecutors charged Zhuoying Chen and Haojie Zhang for their alleged roles in a crime ring that laundered money stolen from cyber investment fraud scams.
  • Chen and Zhang allegedly managed a network of more than a dozen people in Queens and Brooklyn between 2020 and 2022.
  • The criminal network allegedly moved at least $43 million in scam proceeds to bank accounts in China using 140 bank accounts under roughly 45 shell companies.
  • The underlying scams involved contacting potential victims through social media or messaging services, building trust, showing fake profits, and stealing additional funds invested by victims.
  • If convicted of conspiracy to commit money laundering, Chen and Zhang each face a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison.

Three Brands, One Lure: A Chase 'Secure Message via Virtru' That Actually Came From LinkedIn — May Read

A phishing email impersonated a Chase secure message via Virtru while actually using a LinkedIn sender address and Mimecast-wrapped links, creating a three-brand mismatch designed to look trustworthy. The key warning sign was that the visible brand, sender, and link destination did not align, alongside stale and generic message content.

  • A phishing email impersonated Chase with a secure-message template that claimed the recipient had a new secure message via Virtru.
  • The email’s visible Chase branding, claimed Virtru provider, and actual From header of messages-noreply@linkedin.com created three unrelated identities in one message.
  • The call-to-action buttons used real Mimecast URL-protection domains, including a link with a chase.com parameter, instead of pointing directly to Chase.
  • The message contained signs of reused canned content, including an already-expired notice, broken grammar, and a generic ACH_Incoming_Payments label with no personalization.
  • IRONSCALES Themis classified the message as phishing at 90% confidence and remediated it across the affected mailboxes.

Armenia Detains Russian Tourist on U.S. Warrant for REvil Hacker, Lawyers Say Wrong Man — May Read

Armenia detained a Russian tourist named Aleksandr Ermakov on a U.S. extradition request for a suspected REvil ransomware operator, but his lawyers say authorities have confused him with a different Aleksandr Ermakov already serving a sentence in Russia. The case appears to hinge on incomplete identity data in the warrant or Interpol notice, with no public confirmation yet from Armenian or U.S. authorities.

  • Armenia has detained Russian tourist Aleksandr Yuryevich Ermakov since June 28 on a U.S. extradition request for a REvil ransomware suspect named Aleksandr Ermakov.
  • The U.S.-wanted person is identified in sanctions records as Aleksandr Gennadievich Ermakov, who was sanctioned by Australia, the United States, and the United Kingdom in January 2024 over the Medibank Private data theft.
  • Lawyers for the detained man say he is a former prison-service lawyer from Omsk who does not speak English and is not the same person as the sanctioned hacker.
  • Russian reporting cited in the article says Aleksandr Gennadievich Ermakov is serving a two-year Russian sentence that bars him from leaving the country.
  • The article says Armenian authorities have not commented, the U.S. Justice Department has announced no charges, and the detained man is being held on a 30-day Interpol detention order while Moscow seeks consular access.

Windows Server 2022 reach end of mainstream support in 90 days — May Read

Windows Server 2022 will leave mainstream support on October 13, 2026, but will continue receiving free monthly security updates under extended support until October 14, 2031. Microsoft recommends organizations begin planning and testing upgrades to Windows Server 2025 for full mainstream support.

  • Windows Server 2022 will reach the end of mainstream support on October 13, 2026, with the October 2026 security update being the last mainstream support update for this version.
  • After October 13, 2026, Windows Server 2022 will move to extended support and continue receiving monthly security updates at no additional cost through October 14, 2031.
  • Microsoft advises customers to upgrade to Windows Server 2025, the latest Long-Term Servicing Channel release for Windows Server, to receive full mainstream support.
  • Windows Server 2025 became generally available in November 2024 and is available for testing through a free 180-day trial from the Microsoft Evaluation Center.
  • Microsoft extended Windows Server 2022 hotpatching until October 2027 for systems running the Datacenter: Azure Edition.

Zelensky appoints Ukraine's acting security service chief as acting defense minister — May Read

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky named acting SBU chief Yevhenii Khmara as acting defense minister after a cabinet reshuffle sparked protests. Some lawmakers questioned whether the appointment is legal because Ukraine requires the defense minister to be a civilian.

  • Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky named intelligence and counterterrorism official Yevhenii Khmara as acting defense minister after a government reshuffle sparked protests across Ukraine.
  • Zelensky said he would formally ask parliament to approve Khmara as defense minister once the required legal procedures had been completed.
  • Khmara has served as acting head of the Security Service of Ukraine since January and previously led the SBU's Alpha Special Operations Center.
  • Zelensky said Khmara's experience with technology-driven long-range strike operations made him well suited to oversee Ukraine's defense during the war.
  • Several Ukrainian lawmakers questioned whether Khmara's appointment complied with laws requiring the defense minister and deputy defense ministers to be civilians rather than serving military officers.

Inside the Search for "Clean" Residential Proxies for Carding — Optional

Criminal carding actors increasingly see residential proxies as only one fragile part of a broader identity-simulation setup, prioritizing “clean” IP reputation, precise location matching, and browser/device consistency. Defenders should not trust residential traffic by default and should focus on cross-session signals like fingerprints, billing data, behavior, and transaction velocity.

  • Flare researchers analyzed 2,889 unique underground posts from the past two years across about 545 discussion threads about residential proxies and carding.
  • Carders increasingly distinguish between “clean” and “dirty” residential proxy pools based on prior use, reputation scores, and whether financial services have blocked the addresses.
  • Underground discussions show actors trying to match proxy location with stolen identity details such as billing ZIP code, device time zone, operating-system language, and browser characteristics.
  • Residential proxies are frequently discussed alongside antidetect browsers, isolated devices, cookie history, WebRTC configuration, Canvas and WebGL fingerprints, and user-agent consistency.
  • The article says defenders should treat residential traffic as context rather than proof that a user is legitimate, and should evaluate consistency across device history, account age, browser fingerprint, payment information, billing information, transaction velocity, and behavior after checkout.

Top Pentera alternatives for automated penetration testing — Optional

Pentera is strong for automated infrastructure and network security validation, but it does not deeply test application and API logic where fast-shipping teams increasingly face risk. The article positions Aikido Security as the best alternative for AI-driven application-layer pentesting, while Horizon3 NodeZero is the closest direct competitor for infrastructure-focused testing.

  • Pentera is positioned as an automated security validation platform for internal networks, external attack surfaces, and cloud identity paths, with strengths in Active Directory attack chains, credential abuse, lateral movement, and privilege escalation.
  • The article says Pentera does not deeply test application and API logic such as IDORs, business logic flaws, BOLA, or multi-step authenticated flows.
  • Aikido Security is presented as the best choice for teams needing application and API-layer AI pentesting, using autonomous agents and white-box testing to read source code before attacking it.
  • Horizon3 NodeZero is described as the closest direct competitor to Pentera for teams focused on infrastructure and network pentesting.
  • The article argues that fast software release cycles make application-layer testing more important because scheduled manual pentests may miss vulnerabilities introduced between releases or deliver outdated findings.

June Incident Response Insights — Optional

Booz Allen’s June Incident Response Insights Report, promoted by Health-ISAC, offers threat intelligence drawn from more than 1,000 real-world incident response engagements. The main takeaway is that healthcare organizations can use frontline incident data to better understand current attacker behavior and improve resilience.

  • The article announces the June Incident Response Insights report dated July 17, 2026.
  • Booz Allen’s Incident Response Insights Report provides intelligence from more than 1,000 real-world engagements annually.
  • The report focuses on what threat actors are doing, where the threat landscape is headed, and what Booz Allen has encountered on the frontlines during the month.
  • The article describes Booz Allen as a Health-ISAC Community Services Champion.
  • The article presents the report as a resource for cyber threat intelligence based on real incidents rather than theoretical risks.

Black Hat Asia 2026: Cleartext Cookie Exposure | Corelight — Optional

Corelight is highlighting cleartext cookie exposure at Black Hat Asia 2026, emphasizing that unencrypted cookies can leak sensitive session data and create account takeover risk.

  • The article is titled “Black Hat Asia 2026: Cleartext Cookie Exposure | Corelight.”
  • The article references Black Hat Asia 2026.
  • The article references cleartext cookie exposure.
  • The article references Corelight.

The Race to Field Military Autonomy Is On, Can Trusted Information Infrastructure Keep Pace? — Optional

Everfox argues that as the U.S., UK, and NATO accelerate military autonomy, the key challenge is building trusted information infrastructure that lets autonomous systems securely share mission data across platforms, classifications, and coalition partners. The article promotes hardware-enforced separation and cross-domain sharing as the foundation for deploying autonomous capabilities at mission speed.

  • Military forces in the U.S., UK, and NATO are accelerating investment and acquisition efforts for autonomous capabilities across defense programs.
  • The article argues that autonomous systems such as aircraft, maritime vessels, ground systems, satellites, and AI-enabled mission applications depend on trusted information moving securely across platforms, domains, and partners.
  • Programs adopting commercial technologies need information infrastructure that can support rapid deployment without requiring years of bespoke integration work.
  • The article presents hardware-enforced separation as a way to establish trust by relying on hardware logic rather than solely on software controls.
  • Everfox promotes its trusted information platform as a way for defense organizations to securely exchange mission-critical information across systems, classifications, and coalition partners.

item.title: Exploited SharePoint CVE-2026-32201 Chain, Malicious NuGet Packages, and AI Agent Access Risks
